text: Therefore, some workers find it very hard to see how industry transformation can benefit them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Currently, the IGP administered by NTUC's e2i aims to address this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In turn, they are required to share the productivity gains with their workers through higher wages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, as the pace of our industry transformation quickens, we need to do more to encourage companies to move in this direction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is to support SMEs in undertaking deeper and even more ambitious transformation projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These outcomes may include wage increases, job creation, job redesign or hiring of older workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With this change, workers' outcomes will be a mandatory consideration from the very first dollar of the EDG funding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: NTUC and ESG will work closely together on the mechanisms to implement this, and we will announce details later.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, I will now continue in Mandarin, please.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: (In Mandarin):  : The merger of EDG and IDP represents a significant change in how we approach our enterprise transformation efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will encourage companies to think of how to improve their workers' skills and career prospects through transformation right at the start when companies design their transformation plans and apply for Government grants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: After merger, from 1 April 2020 onwards, NTUC, the unions and ESG will work together to ensure improved productivity is translated into better worker outcomes, such as wage increases, job creation or hiring of older workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Through this change, we hope to send a strong signal about the Government's commitment to work closely with the Labour Movement to keep People at the heart of our transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: (In English): On Mr Chen Show Mao's query, the inclusion of worker outcomes into the enhanced EDG will be complemented by the efforts of the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers which was established last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This Workgroup is studying issues relating to older workers, including how to make workplaces more conducive for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Workgroup's recommendations will be released later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, many of the suggestions by Mr Chen Show Mao are not new and have already been implemented on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, our Labour Movement's push to implement more company training committees will be one mechanism in which the Labour Movement can work with companies to ensure that workers' outcomes, including older workers', are taken into account when the company transforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We put people at the heart of our industry transformation because they are our nation’s most valuable asset.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: By partnering unions and businesses, we can translate economic growth into real opportunities and better outcomes for all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Chairman, business leaders must take the lead in enterprise transformation, as they know their business and customers best.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The Government will provide customised support through our enterprise development schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: As Minister Chan Chun Sing said, our efforts are centred around three "Ups": Level Up, to strengthen companies' capabilities; Scale Up, to help enterprises grow in Singapore and abroad; and Team Up, to encourage companies to work together for win-win outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Teo Ser Luck suggested that companies must level up and strengthen their capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Enterprise transformation must start with its people, to redesign jobs and upskill workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Transformation may be technology-driven, but it should remain human-centric and people-led.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Earlier, the Minister shared that we will enhance PSG to support employer-led training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is on top of existing SkillsFuture subsidies and the funding for pre-scoped productivity solutions under PSG.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: MTI will work with SSG on the implementation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Another priority is to encourage companies to make good use of technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Regardless of size and sector, all companies need to embrace technology as a tool to improve productivity, reduce operating costs and develop better products and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Low Thia Khiang suggested having more public sector research flow into industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: MTI has been doing this under the RIE2020 Plan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We want to grow these numbers over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For example, optronics technology which originated from defence research was used by an SME to measure water quality in our reservoirs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: There is scope to explore having more of such collaborations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: However, I am sure Mr Low Thia Khiang would agree that not everything from defence research can flow into the commercial sector, as some are classified projects to protect national security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Enterprises can also re-engineer their business processes by harnessing the value of design and using design thinking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I look forward to welcoming Design Singapore to the MTI family from 1 April.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We can further strengthen the synergies with economic agencies to grow design capabilities in our enterprises and workforce and use design as an enabler to improve Singapore’s competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Next, we will support companies on their growth journeys to Scale Up their operations locally and overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We have built a vibrant startup ecosystem through a range of measures, such as financing, networks, infrastructure and mentorship.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To succeed, we must remain open to ideas and talent, including attracting overseas startups and entrepreneurs, to operate here and use Singapore as a hub for the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Several Members have made this point as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: A number of our startups originate from the universities and polytechnics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I am encouraged to see young Singaporeans stepping forward to start their own business and turning their passion into possibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The nature of the industry is such that a few will succeed but many will fail, and some may even fail repeatedly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: But this is part of the learning process and what we need to build an enterprising society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It includes a "never-say-die" attitude, the courage to take calculated risks and the resourcefulness to translate innovative ideas into reality.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For enterprises that are ready to expand beyond Singapore, we will help them to develop their internationalisation capabilities and expand into overseas markets, tapping on our extensive FTA networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For many years, IE Singapore, now ESG, has been supporting our companies in foreign markets through its overseas offices, working closely with EDB and other Government agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For companies that have internationalised, overseas revenue forms nearly half of their total revenue and has grown more quickly than local revenue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The overseas markets have greater potential for growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We worked with partners to help our companies enter new markets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Last year, ESG added eight new partners to its Plug and Play Network, which has recently expanded to two new countries, the United Arab Emirates and Cambodia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: As Ms Cheryl Chan highlighted, these initiatives and partnerships provide large firms and SMEs with in-market support to help them with their overseas expansion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We have seen Singapore companies taking on more ambitious projects overseas, which entail larger investments over longer periods of time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: While these efforts may reap long-term returns in the future, banks may be hesitant to provide financing, given the higher level of risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The Government will increase our support for these projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In his Budget speech, the Minister for Finance announced the new Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS), which will be launched this October.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: EFS brings ESG's financing schemes under a common umbrella scheme, making it easier for our companies to access financing support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will also provide a higher risk share for enterprises venturing into challenging markets, as they do face higher hurdles in obtaining financing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I agree with Miss Cheryl Chan that we should provide tailored support to nurture local enterprises that can grow and contribute significantly to our economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Minister Chan Chun Sing mentioned the Scale-up SG programme to groom high-growth enterprises into future global champions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Through this programme, we will help enterprises develop and implement long-term plans tailored to their specific growth priorities in areas, such as innovation and international expansion.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For instance, a healthcare services company with overseas operations may aim to double its footprint through M&A and expand upstream by developing its own products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Through Scale-up SG, the company will receive targeted support to develop a commercially viable product prototype, as well as to shortlist and validate acquisition targets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: When these companies grow and succeed in future, I hope they will also provide opportunities to other local companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In this way, we can sustain our scale-up efforts and grow more Singapore companies into globally competitive enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: As noted by Mr Teo Ser Luck and Mr Leon Perera, collaborations among enterprises can support capability development to testbed innovative solutions and form business alliances to capture opportunities here and overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For example, Rolls-Royce and KA Industrial Engineering, a local SME, have worked together on an automated system for loading and unloading fan blades.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Previously, the process was carried out by multiple technicians dressed in protective suits, due to the high temperatures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: With the automated system, a single technician can manage the process, away from the furnace, improving both productivity and worker safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Importantly, working with Rolls-Royce helps KA Industrial Engineering open doors to other clients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Partnerships can be amongst enterprises of all sizes and with TACs, too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We enhanced Partnerships for Capability Transformation (PACT) last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This will continue to support collaborations between enterprises of all sizes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I encourage companies to band together to tap on PACT to benefit from one another's strengths, develop deeper capabilities and successfully internationalise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our conversations cannot start with Government agencies telling companies to buy equipment, adopt information technology (IT) solutions or appoint consultants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We should not pretend that we know what each firm needs to improve its products and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: That must come from the business owner, based on a good understanding of what his or her customers require.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Likewise, businesses should not begin the conversation by asking what grants they can obtain from the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We want to encourage entrepreneurs, not grantrepreneurs who seek to maximise their grant amount instead of focusing on how they want to transform and grow their business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Enterprise transformation must start with a vision of what the business wants to achieve, what problems it wants to solve and what capabilities it needs to build to reach its goals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Then we look at what schemes and grants can best support the company.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our efforts must be enterprise-centric and transformation-focused, not scheme-centric and grant-focused.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: MTI will continue to work with other Government agencies and industry partners to review our policies and processes to achieve this outcome.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We believe this is effective in helping businesses to build deep capabilities and for Singapore to grow a thicker layer of fast-growing local companies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Mr Chairman, for broad-based economic success, the Government cannot do it alone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Our TACs are crucial partners on this journey.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: TACs are a store of social capital – institutional memory, industry networks, access to overseas markets.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: TACs help the Government to better understand the needs of our business community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: To Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Douglas Foo’s queries, we support our TACs to broaden the reach of our ITMs and drive industry projects through the LEAD programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Last year, the Association of SMEs launched the SME Cloud Exchange Network Software (SMECEN) with LEAD support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: This is a cloud-based platform for companies to perform accounting and human resource functions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: In 2017, LEAD was expanded to support a larger base of TACs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: I encourage our TACs to play an even stronger role.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: ESG will develop five-year roadmaps with TACs to help our TACs adopt a longer-term strategy to drive industry transformation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: For example, ESG is developing a roadmap with SBF to help our local businesses access overseas markets.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: We will support TACs to implement the roadmaps through the LEAD programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: This includes seconding our public officers to selected TACs to allow our officers to better understand our businesses' concerns as we work together as one Team Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat spoke about developing our enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: As the Minister for Finance said during the Budget Debate, the Government must be prepared to experiment and take calculated risks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: This applies to our regulations, which Mr Baey Yam Keng and Mr Lee Yi Shyan touched upon.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: First, we must create an environment where new business ideas can take flight.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: One way is through regulatory sandboxes, where companies can learn quickly, iterate quickly.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: This has enabled new business concepts like dining in a "Floating Donut" in Marina Bay.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: When the idea was first raised or first floated, agencies had public safety and pollution concerns.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: But with the sandbox in place, the company was allowed to test their business concept for six months, with necessary safeguards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Second, we want to streamline regulations to reduce costs, cut paperwork and free up resources.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: This is a progressive economic policy move because it is the smaller businesses which have fewer resources to navigate regulations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Third, we will make it easier for businesses to apply for licences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Starting with the food services sector, we will pilot a one-stop portal to help automate the application process and cut down processing time as far as possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: For example, the portal will automatically recommend a course of action for land use approvals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: This will save companies the hassle of going to different agencies' websites to find out the approved land use of a particular place.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: For example, the requirement to affix company stamps on Government forms has been removed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: We agree with companies' feedback that this was outdated, unnecessary, cumbersome and time-consuming.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: However, the suggestion of imposing a "sunset clause" on regulations may be too prescriptive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: What is more important is a mindset where agencies are continuously alive – alive to the idea of rules review, alive to the idea of adapting, alive to the idea of transformation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: A living culture of asking "why do we have this rule?", "is the rule still needed?", "is there a better way of doing things?" Because governance is not always about adding more rules.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Sometimes, we need to tidy up to spark innovation; and, sometimes, we need to tidy up to spark joy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Besides supporting our enterprises, we want well-functioning markets that help consumers benefit from more choices and more competitive prices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Under the Open Electricity Market (OEM), households and small businesses now have more choices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: At the same time, we will ensure that consumers’ interests are protected.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: For example, retailers have to consistently hedge at least 50% of their wholesale electricity price risk.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Retailers must also safeguard all security deposits collected from household consumers and return them to these household consumers should a retailer exit the market.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: EMA also has safeguards in place to prevent retailers from unilaterally terminating contracts, unless the retailer is exiting the market or the consumer has breached the contract terms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Retailers who wish to exit the market are expected to find other retailers to take on those consumers on the same terms and conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: If the retailer cannot find a replacement or if the consumer rejects the proposed transfer, the supply of electricity to the consumer will not be disrupted as the consumer will be transferred to SP Group.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Mr Pritam Singh asked about the retailer who had been selling electricity to the Aljunied-Hougang Town Council.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: I hear Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Teo Ser Luck's feedback on instalment plans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: In my own constituency duties, I have seen similar situations with my residents and, in my previous role as a backbencher, I have filed Parliamentary Questions on related topics as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Today, most consumer credit providers, such as moneylenders and financial institutions, are already regulated.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Such providers have to adhere to rules, including borrowing limits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: I agree that there should be adequate information disclosure by retailers so that consumers can make informed decisions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Enticement of consumers to over-leverage on credit should not be allowed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: MoneySENSE, the national financial education programme, also provides consumers with tips on what they should look out for when taking loans and instalments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: On Mr Lim Biow Chuan's suggestion, the Government has to balance between consumers' interests and a pro-enterprise environment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: A broad-based cooling off period may potentially be subject to abuse and introduce uncertainty to businesses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: There are also challenges, some quite complex, in defining the arena of "beauty and slimming" services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: CASE and the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS) have conducted outreach activities to educate consumers on what our consumers should watch out for before committing to purchases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: ABS has also developed Frequently Asked Questions on chargeback.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: MAS will continue to work with stakeholders to educate consumers on their rights and obligations when making purchases using credit cards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: If you are not sure, do not be afraid to ask.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: What kind of financial commitments are in the contract?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Think about buying from CaseTrust businesses which offer a cooling off period.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: (In Mandarin):  : We also want consumers to access information more easily and compare options, and save money, time and effort.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: MTI is working with CASE to develop a crowdsourcing app for consumers to compare prices for groceries and cooked food.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Through this app, consumers are able to share price information which benefits the wider community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Those with less time, less awareness of market prices, and less purchasing experience, will benefit the most.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: As for seniors without smartphones, they can still benefit through hearing of good bargains from neighbours, family members or friends who use the app.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: (In English): In conclusion, economic transformation is a collective effort.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: It takes all of us – Government, businesses, TACs and our workers – our brothers and sisters in the Labour Movement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: It takes all of us, working together, to transform our economy to succeed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Let us continue working together to create good jobs, better opportunities and a bright future for Singapore and all our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, probably it is timely to ask him on the latest progress of the RCEP negotiations.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: We have a few elections in the region in the member states.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Is there enough political will to overcome the specific sensitive issues and do we have reasons to be optimistic for the agreement to be concluded this year?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chairman, let me thank Mr Liang Eng Hwa for his question.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Yes, indeed, I just came back from Cambodia.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In Cambodia over the weekend, the Ministers had a good discussion on RCEP.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: More so than last year, they understand the strategic significance of RCEP and also the criticality of the timing of RCEP.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In a world where we see the rise of protectionism, unilateral moves by various countries and so forth, many in Southeast Asia and in the rest of Asia see the urgency to try to conclude this, not just for the economic benefits alone but also because of the positive message we want to send to the rest of the world of how we collectively believe in greater integration for the greater good of our peoples.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Under Thailand's ASEAN chairmanship, we see this as a very positive development.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: However, as Mr Liang Eng Hwa said, there are a few uncertainties.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: From now till the end of May, these four countries will be very involved in their domestic elections.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: What the Ministers have directed the negotiators to focus on is to make sure that we clear as much of the technical issues as possible from now till June.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This will be a critical milestone because this will be a point where we will make the political decision and show the political commitment that all the 16 countries want to get it done this year.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, the first part of the year, we will see the frontloading of the technical aspects of the work.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In the third quarter of this year, we hope to see a resolution on the political direction after the completion of the four regional elections.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In the meantime, the respective working groups are working hard to close off the remaining chapters and the technical issues.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Just following up with the clarification from Senior Parliamentary Secretary Tan Wu Ming on electricity retailers.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I understand in the event a retailer exits from the market in the household sector, the retailer will be required, as per Senior Parliamentary Secretary's answer, to provide electricity or to find a retailer who would provide electricity at the same price.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: In the event that fails, I do not believe that Senior Parliamentary Secretary Tan has clarified what compensation alternatives would be available to the residents, given that they would be back on the standard SP tariff rate.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: In case I missed that, just a query.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: From the viewpoint of household consumers, one of the key objectives in the OEM is that in the event a retailer exits, that household continues to receive electricity.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: As a first instance, if a retailer is exiting, they are expected to try and find an alternative supplier for that household with equivalent terms or, failing which, if the alternative cannot be found, the household reverts to SP Group as the provider of last resort in such a situation.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Mr Pritam Singh also raised a separate question, which is, whether there is a concept of expectation loss here.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: It is worth bearing in mind that in the current operating environment, where households may have obtained discounted rates from an electricity supplier, and subsequently, if the supplier exits, and they revert to SP Group, they have obtained savings at that point.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, I am just wondering what Mr Pritam Singh means by seeking compensation.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: If I can put it in a different way.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Right now, let us say, the shoe is on the other foot and the consumer decides to move on to another retailer, because the rates are more favourable than the existing rate that the consumer has bargained for.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: What would happen is they have to pay a termination fee and I am just wondering if there is a similar mechanism if it was the other way round.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: That is essentially the essence of my question.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, there are actually two distinct scenarios in that one question which Mr Pritam Singh has raised.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: One scenario is, if the retailer is still in the market and the consumer decides to initiate termination of the contract, and to move to another retailer because of a better deal.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: In that situation, if the consumer is the one initiating the termination and moving to a different supplier, then those terms and conditions, whether there is an early termination fee, would apply.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: But, in the event of the other situation, when a retailer chooses to exit the market, firstly, as I mentioned earlier, the retailer has to source around to see if another retailer will offer an equivalent plan to the existing consumers.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: In that situation, even then, the consumer can decide he does not like this alternative because there is another better alternative available in the market when the existing retailer exits, the consumer still has that choice.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, it depends on which situation Mr Pritam Singh is looking at for the purposes of this question.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: First, whether the ongoing issue with Malaysia, namely, the airspace and the port issues, if they remain unsolved, would they affect Singapore's economy?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: The second clarification is whether the Minister sees the defence industry having the potential to contribute to the Singapore economy.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chairman, let me thank Mr Low Thia Khiang for his two clarifications.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, there is some cross-pollination of ideas and benefits in growing ST Engineering companies.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And there are examples that my colleagues have given just now.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The defence industry, either directly or indirectly, through the use of the related technologies, can benefit the wider economy.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On Mr Low Thia Khiang's first question about the impact of the issues with Malaysia on the Singapore economy, there are two levels that we must always bear in mind.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Our position is that we continue to look for win-win situations and win-win projects together with Malaysia because we always believe that a prosperous Malaysia that is doing well economically is good for Malaysia, is good for the region.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We will continue on this mode, this kind of mental model that we are seeking win-win cooperation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We asked and encouraged our companies to diversify their sources, their supply chains and their markets.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is part of our wider strategy to ensure that we will never be held ransom by any one particular market for our supply chains or for the market for our products and services.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, this, we must continue to do, regardless of whether it is Malaysia or any one particular market.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But the Member is right, Malaysia is our next-door neighbour, our closest neighbour.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because they are our closest neighbour, all the more we must make sure that we continue to diversify and take this issue very seriously, that our economy is never held ransom or dependent on a single source.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: I just wanted to ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary, we already have a mandatory cooling-off period for purchase of timeshare contracts.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: There is also what they call a free-look period for life and health insurance products.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary give a compelling reason why MTI is not prepared to consider a cooling-off period for contracts with businesses in the beauty and slimming industry?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: First of these is whether the extent of commitment by the individual consumer is very substantial and whether there have been legitimate opportunities for the consumer to decline entering into a contract at that point in time.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I hear what the Member said about how someone going for a massage finds himself under the wrong kind of pressure.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: But we also have to bear in mind that if a consumer feels they have been wrongfully confined, if someone is trying to extract certain decisions or concessions while they are in a vulnerable position, a consumer can and should consider asking for the authorities to be alerted.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: If someone locks you in a room and asks you to sign a contract, I think Mr Lim Biow Chuan, being a lawyer, he also knows what the options are available.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And you do not necessarily need to call in a lawyer for that.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: But more broadly, I would say there is also the need for us, throughout society, to continue sending a message, not just looking at legislative measures but also as a community of consumers and concerned citizens, about what kind of sales tactics are acceptable, unacceptable or completely beyond the pale in our society.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, would you like to withdraw your amendment, please?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: He used to be helping and supporting entrepreneurs and startups when he was in MTI, and now he is himself an entrepreneur and a startup.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, this is an indication of our vibrant startup scene.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: We can only now wish MTI and the economic agencies every success.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: With that, I beg leave to withdraw the amendment, Sir.
